title: Restriction of the direct image to bounded constructibles
statement:
Let $\Lambda=P_n$ be as in
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness], let $u:S\to T$ be a
morphism of schemes, and suppose $\mathrm{FIN}(u,\Lambda;c)$. Then the
ambient functor $Ru_*$ restricts to an exact triangulated functor
$$
 Ru_*:\Dbc(S_{\Proet},\Lambda)\longrightarrow\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\Lambda),
$$
and if $K\in\Dbc(S_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$, then
$Ru_*K$ has cohomology in $[a,b+c]$.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this conditional restriction.
Stacks' constructibility entries are Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)) and Proposition 61.29.7
([Tag 09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)), stated on a
Noetherian scheme for a Noetherian coefficient ring, together with Lemma
61.29.2 ([Tag 09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)), which
realizes one constructible $K$ as $\Rlim K_n$ with each $K_n$ of bounded tor
amplitude, constructible cohomology and etale origin; the finiteness and
amplitude inputs are Lemma 59.92.2 ([Tag
095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U): for $f$ proper with all
fibres of dimension $\le n$ and every abelian torsion sheaf $\mathcal F$ on
$X_{\Et}$ one has $R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$ for $q>2n$) and Theorem 63.14.5 ([Tag
0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0): for $f$ separated of
finite presentation and $K\in D^+_{tors,c}(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $Rf_!K$ has
constructible cohomology sheaves). Difference: both are etale-site
statements about a single coefficient ring, with no amplitude shift, no
uniformity over a coefficient tower and no pro-etale site; the blueprint
adds the transport of these conditions to the small pro-etale sites as the
predicate $\mathrm{FIN}(u,\Lambda;c)$ and the amplitude shift by $c$.

proof.text: By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], the canonical coefficient structure map $u^{-1}\Lambda_{T,\Proet}\to\Lambda_{S,\Proet}$ is an isomorphism. Use this identification in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Use the small-site universe convention in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For $V=S,T$, the category $\Mod(\Lambda_{V,\Proet})$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. The section formula for $u_*$ in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and sectionwise kernels in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] show directly that $u_*$ is additive and preserves kernels: evaluation on each $W$ gives the kernel of the same module map evaluated on $S\times_TW$. It is therefore left exact. On bounded below objects the ordinary unbounded $Ru_*$ agrees with the bounded below right derived functor by [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing], with lower bound $0$, applies to $F[0]$ for any module sheaf $F$, and gives $\mathcal H^j(Ru_*(F[0]))=0$ for $j<0$.

source.place: Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing (1); ordinary K-injective derived operations as specified in the cited definitions

proof.text: Fix $K\in\Dbc(S_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ with cohomology in $[a,b]$. If $a>b$, all cohomology of $K$ vanishes, so $K$ is zero in the localization at quasi-isomorphisms and its additive derived image is zero; hence assume $a\leq b$. The ring $\Lambda=P_n$ is finite commutative (in particular Noetherian, since it has only finitely many ideals), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] applies with no extra hypothesis on $S$: every $F_q=\mathcal H^q(K)$ is intrinsically constructible, and it vanishes outside $[a,b]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-sheaf-origin], each $F_q$ is the pullback of a constructible etale sheaf, hence is constructible in precisely the meaning used in [def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness]. The same two comparison statements apply on $T$.

For each $q\in[a,b]$, clause 1 of $\mathrm{FIN}(u,\Lambda;c)$ says that $\mathcal H^p(Ru_*(F_q[0]))$ is constructible for $p\geq0$, and clause 2 says that it is zero for $p>c$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness]. Step 1 supplies zero cohomology for $p<0$. By the sheaf comparison [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-sheaf-origin], these nonzero cohomology sheaves are intrinsically constructible; by the derived comparison [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], $Ru_*(F_q[0])$ therefore belongs to $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ and has interval $[0,c]$. The ambient functor is triangulated [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], so $Ru_*(F_q[-q])\cong(Ru_*(F_q[0]))[-q]$. Since $\mathcal H^i(M[-q])=\mathcal H^{i-q}(M)$, this image has interval $[q,q+c]$.

source.place: Tags 09AK and 09AL; FIN clauses 1 and 2 from the blueprint definition

proof.text: Put $K_j=\tau_{\leq j}K$ for $a-1\leq j\leq b$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $K_{a-1}$ is acyclic, hence is zero in the derived category, and $K_b\to K$ is a quasi-isomorphism, hence an isomorphism. Apply [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] to $K_j$ at $j$. Its first object is $\tau_{\leq j-1}K_j=K_{j-1}$, by the explicit kernel truncation in [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology]: below degree $j-1$ both complexes agree with $K$, and in degree $j-1$ the kernel of $K^{j-1}\to\ker(d_K^j)$ is $\ker(d_K^{j-1})$, since $\ker(d_K^j)\to K^j$ is monic; all higher terms are zero. The first triangle map is the canonical truncation inclusion. Its third object $C_j$ has cohomology only in degree $j$, where it is $F_j$: the triangle statement gives $\mathcal H^i(C_j)=0$ for $i<j$; at $i=j$ the long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] has $0=\mathcal H^j(K_{j-1})\to F_j\to\mathcal H^j(C_j)\to\mathcal H^{j+1}(K_{j-1})=0$, so its middle map is an isomorphism; for $i>j$ the same sequence has $\mathcal H^i(K_j)=0$ and $\mathcal H^{i+1}(K_{j-1})=0$ on either side of $\mathcal H^i(C_j)$, so it vanishes. By [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single], $C_j\cong F_j[-j]$. We obtain distinguished triangles $K_{j-1}\to K_j\to F_j[-j]\to K_{j-1}[1]$ for every $a\leq j\leq b$.

Induct on $j=a-1,a,\ldots,b$. The induction claim for $j\geq a$ is that $Ru_*K_j$ belongs to $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ and has cohomology in $[a,j+c]$; the initial object $Ru_*K_{a-1}$ is zero because the ambient functor is additive [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Apply that triangulated functor to the triangle in step 4. Its outer objects $Ru_*K_{j-1}$ and $Ru_*(F_j[-j])$ are bounded constructible by induction and step 3. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] identifies this property with bounded intrinsically constructible cohomology, and [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] gives that property for the middle object. The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] proves its interval: if $i<a$ or $i>j+c$, both outer degree-$i$ cohomology objects are zero (for $j=a$, the first outer object is simply zero), so exactness forces $\mathcal H^i(Ru_*K_j)=0$. At $j=b$ use $K_b\cong K$ to obtain $Ru_*K\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ with interval $[a,b+c]$.

source.place: Tag 08J5, finite induction on the successive truncation triangles; Tag 09AL for constructible triangulated closure

proof.text: For $V=S,T$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] and [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] identify the category $\Dbc(V_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] with a strictly full triangulated subcategory of its ambient derived category. Step 5 shows that the ambient $Ru_*$ maps the source subcategory into the target. Restrict it on objects and on all morphisms. Its ambient shift isomorphisms restrict because the subcategories are full and closed under shifts, and its images of distinguished triangles are distinguished in the target subcategory because they are distinguished in the ambient category. Hence the restricted functor is exact triangulated, by the triangulatedness of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations].

split_report.summary: Replaced the implicit spectral-sequence/Serre argument by finite canonical-truncation induction. Explicitly transported between etale-origin and intrinsic constructibility for the general finite commutative ring P_n, supplied negative vanishing and bounded/unbounded derived compatibility, and proved the amplitude and exact restriction. No statement change and no new nodes.
